title: This app is making $2,000 PER DAY

speakers.name: Gus (co-host and producer of Starter Story)

promo_conflict: Starter Story uses the episode to promote its own paid database of simple app ideas (L52, L251). The intro says '$23,000 a day' (L2), which conflicts with the guest's '$2,000 to $3,000 a day' (L26) and the dashboard figure of about $2,000 a day (L69). L2 is probably a transcription or editing error.

stated_problem.quote: I feel like if you deal with crypto, a lot of people have wallet keys, storing all sorts of places.
stated_problem.speaker: Rastie Turek

idea.name: Voltaire encrypted vault iOS app
idea.one_liner: A free iPhone app that encrypts and stores files and photos on the device, such as crypto wallet keys, ID photos and birth certificates. It makes money from cheap weekly, annual and lifetime upgrades, and growth comes from AI-agent-run SEO guides.
idea.customer: Privacy- and security-minded iPhone users, including crypto holders storing wallet keys and people storing ID documents
idea.offer: Encrypted vault on the device with no servers and no shared keys, opened by a pattern; advanced features are paid
idea.revenue_model: Freemium in-app purchases: $1.99 weekly, $19.99 annual, $39.99 lifetime. About 60% of purchases and over 80% of revenue are lifetime

key_quotes.quote: I build Voltaire, which is iPhone app and encrypts the storage and allows people to store encrypted files and photos.
It's encrypted on device, there's no servers, no shared keys.
Most of the apps in this area are 15 years or older.
And so my approach was like, what if I try to pull in every keyword that is out there, that essentially points to the same thing as an app store, but on the web.
Everything is done by one of the coding agents.
it runs through keyboard planner every single morning, looks at all the traffic, it identifies keywords that are being surfaced, but not essentially being driven to the site.
This was my solution for it, especially pictures of IDs, birth certificates.

acquisition_channels.details: A marketing site plus daily 'how do I store my photos on iPhone'-style guides. Agents write them using Google Keyword Planner data to find keywords with impressions but no clicks, then optimise internal links and place CTAs where readers tend to drop off. This brings about 10% web conversion and is now most of the traffic.
Organic Apple App Store search. Downloads come mainly from Apple search, and there are no paid ads.

ideas.delivery: A native iOS app with on-device encryption and no backend, using iCloud/native features. A Claude coding agent wrote all of the code and site content and runs the daily SEO loop. PostHog handles measurement for free.

tools: 'context' (likely another coding agent; unclear in the transcript)
gum (own open-source CLI/MCP over Google services)

ideas.other_uk_rules: Weekly and annual auto-renewing subscriptions fall under the DMCC Act 2024 subscription-contract rules (clear pre-contract info, reminders, easy cancellation). Apple handles billing, but the seller is still responsible for disclosures. UK GDPR exposure is minimal because there is no server-side data, though web analytics and cookies on the marketing site need PECR consent. Because data can't be recovered, the app needs clear consumer disclosures, and UK law-enforcement requests (Investigatory Powers Act) may come in.
